issue.body: A failed rewind can leave files, the provider conversation, and T3 history at different checkpoints. Retrying a relative provider rollback can remove more history. Save each rewind step before moving on. Retry the same checkpoint to finish after a failure or restart. Keep a safety Git ref until the history commit succeeds, and block new thread operations while recovery is pending. Codex forks at the saved checkpoint turn ID without changing or resuming the source conversation. It preserves active goals without running them. Missing native IDs stop the rewind before files change. This requires Codex 0.153.0 or later. OpenCode rewind is temporarily blocked because saved checkpoints do not identify its exact native conversation boundary. Safe rewind is unavailable for Claude, Cursor, Grok, and Antigravity because their adapters cannot preserve the required native history. Stacked on [#10294](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10294) for typed lifecycle completion and the earlier server fixes. The parent includes migration 48. This PR adds migration 49. Git ref cleanup is best effort. A crash after the durable restore commit can retain obsolete refs. User files and the provider conversation are already consistent. ## Verification - 172 focused tests passed. Covers failure after file restore, cursor adoption, restart recovery, exact native boundaries, and blocked commands. - 17 integration tests passed. One existing test is skipped. - After review fixes, 132 focused and integration tests passed, with one existing skip. This includes reactor restart recovery and bounded provider errors. - Restacked onto the final lifecycle parent. All 11 rewind commits are unchanged. The restack passed 224 focused and integration tests, then 150 tests after the parent request-correlation fix. Each run had one existing skip. - Server typecheck and targeted lint passed. Lint has eight existing unused-parameter warnings. - Disposable native Codex 0.153.4 check passed. Partial and empty forks kept an active goal with no model requests or source/config changes. ## Client check A synthetic browser session switched from Codex to OpenCode using capability data from a disposable local server. The Codex rewind control is enabled. The OpenCode action is absent. No rewind command or provider session ran during this check. The native Codex fixture above is separate proof. | Codex | OpenCode | | --- | --- | | ![Codex rewind control enabled](https://files.tslop.org/2026/09/rewind-codex-control-6e63bd69.png) | ![OpenCode rewind action absent](https://files.tslop.org/2026/09/rewind-opencode-blocked-4e2c4db1.png) | Created with Codex. Closes #8958 > [!NOTE] > ### Recover interrupted checkpoint reverts with staged, persistent rollback attempts > - Checkpoint reverts now execute as resumable staged attempts persisted in `checkpoint_revert_attempts`; failures after file or conversation mutation retain the attempt and emit a recovery-required activity instead of a terminal failure > - Conversation rollback moves from a single-step call to a three-stage `prepareConversationRollback` / `forkConversation` / `rollbackConversation` flow across [ProviderService.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10299/files#diff-b9b9384b78856ff56cff5dd0ccb106054fb5d2d1b7500fcd30d8938ebfec5775), with Codex adapter support added in [CodexConversationRollback.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10299/files#diff-37fe083ca13bbd35e359591f26d1b805a1427deadb1f2e4cbc0bd2836d6240d2) > - `OrchestrationEngine` rejects conflicting thread mutations while a revert is unfinished, reserving revert state before command acknowledgment > - `TurnCheckpointCapture` coordinates provider turn termination with checkpoint file capture, blocking subsequent turns until the prior capture completes > - Orchestration projections now carry typed pending-operation state (turn vs compact) across the full lifecycle; shared `derivePendingRequests` consolidates approval and user-input derivation from web and mobile into [pendingRequests.ts](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/10299/files#diff-301834b20cf74929c3fffdc40f7da55f6c4b3f083dfa07f4956b084bce79ea1e) > - Risk: rollback API is a breaking change — callers must use `prepareConversationRollback` + `forkConversation` + `rollbackConversation` instead of the removed single-step method; migration 049 adds the `checkpoint_revert_attempts` table; older snapshots without `pendingOperation` fields fall back to legacy timestamp-based matching > > > > Macroscope summarized 9e29383. > >

comments.body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Fable 5.1 responding on behalf of Theo**

Closing. #8958 is real and worth fixing, but this turns rewind off on OpenCode, Claude, Cursor and Grok (all of which work on main) to make Codex rewind crash-safe, adds a persisted seven-stage state machine in a new table, blocks nine command types from OrchestrationEngine.dispatch by reading a side table, stores untyped provider state in SQLite, and requires Codex 0.153.0. The proportionate fix for #8958 is to run assertConversationRollbackSupported plus a native target check before restoreCheckpoint, and reorder so provider rollback runs before file restore. Happy to take that as a fresh PR.
